operator_io_quirks: All three tables are EMPTY (rows=0): original_values empty, original_sizes all 0; literal pool is the only value source.

DDL has a missing comma between the two FOREIGN KEY clauses in LOCATION (line 'references `GEOGRAPHIC`("CITY_NAME")\nforeign key ...'); sqlite_master stores it verbatim, so CREATE TABLE replay must tolerate it (sqlite accepts it as one FK clause? verify) — do not reformat DDL.
FK parent column names are backtick-quoted in DDL (`GEOGRAPHIC`) while table names are double-quoted; pragma foreign_key_list is the source of truth, not DDL text.

LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID declares FK to RESTAURANT.RESTAURANT_ID, but RESTAURANT's PK column is named ID — parent column RESTAURANT_ID does NOT exist; upstream would assert, spec says DROP with warning. This is a dangling FK.

LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID is also the PK of LOCATION and an FK child: self-consistent only if parent values exist; with empty parent it becomes NULL, but PK NULL is allowed in sqlite (non-INTEGER PK) — rows may survive.
RESTAURANT.ID is INT PRIMARY KEY (rowid alias): inserting NULL auto-assigns rowid; inserting duplicate fails. TS Number fuzzer will produce duplicates -> rows dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
GEOGRAPHIC.CITY_NAME is TEXT PK (non-integer): NULL PK allowed by sqlite; TS String fuzzer rarely emits NULL but contaminate can produce near-duplicates.
Mixed case: table names UPPER, column names UPPER, but DDL uses double quotes; identifiers must be quoted with original case in generated SQL.
RATING is REAL -> Number fuzzer with scale from type args (none) => default scale; values in [-10^s,10^s] floats, perturbed by +-0.01/0.02 — implausible for a 0-5 rating.
HOUSE_NUMBER INT -> Number fuzzer, full int range, perturbed +-1/2 — implausible street numbers (negative, huge).
No views, triggers, indexes beyond PKs; no CHECK/UNIQUE column constraints; notnull=0 everywhere so NOT NULL never enforced.
All tables tiny/empty: choose_table_sizes will pick 1..~2500 rows; no huge-table sampling path exercised.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer for CITY_NAME/COUNTY/REGION/NAME/FOOD_TYPE/STREET_NAME: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop) — names look like 'aB3(x' not 'Berkeley'.
Number fuzzer for ID/RESTAURANT_ID/HOUSE_NUMBER: uniform ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-1/2 perturbation; RATING floats in [-10^s,10^s] +-0.01 — ratings like -437.2.

FK fill: RESTAURANT.CITY_NAME and LOCATION.CITY_NAME draw from GEOGRAPHIC.CITY_NAME final values with replacement; LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID draws from RESTAURANT.RESTAURANT_ID which is dangling -> empty parent -> NULLs (spec 3.4).
PK dedup: RESTAURANT.ID and LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID duplicates dropped (first kept); GEOGRAPHIC.CITY_NAME duplicates dropped.
Likely FN driver: implausible values (negative ratings, garbage city names) make gold queries return empty/odd results, so mutants that should differ look equal.

Likely FP driver: with empty originals, literal pool from train SQL is the only anchor; if pool is sparse, TS values cluster and ties/duplicates appear that the original lacks, causing spurious equalities.

Dangling FK LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID -> RESTAURANT.RESTAURANT_ID: upstream asserts and crashes; spec drops it, so LOCATION.RESTAURANT_ID becomes a plain Number column (not FK-filled) — behaviour differs from a 'correct' schema.

GEOGRAPHIC empty + String fuzzer: CITY_NAME values are random strings, so joins RESTAURANT->GEOGRAPHIC mostly match only via FK fill (same values), but gold queries filtering on real city names return empty.

RATING REAL with no scale arg: Number scale defaults (likely 0 or 4 per spec 3.3 rule 3 only for date/timestamp; for real family scale from args, none => default) — verify; either way values implausible for 0-5.
No CHECK constraints, so checked=False everywhere; p stays 0.2 (or 0 w.p. 0.3 at instance level).
